_source: IBM Bob 2.3.0, /Applications/IBM Bob.app/Contents/Resources/app/extensions/bob-code/dist/extension.js. Each tool is Bob's own getDescription() and getParameters() text, built into an OpenAI function tool the way Bob's own converter does it. The workspace path is a stand-in: /Users/dev/projects/my-app. No user content. Not shortened. Limits: one mode's tool set, no MCP tools; the tests add a one-line system prompt, and do not cover a mode switch mid-task.

function.name: read_file
function.description: Request to read the contents of a file. Supports text files (line-numbered output), images (PNG, JPG, GIF, WebP — displayed for visual analysis and content extraction), PDF (passed directly for reading). Use this to visually examine image-based documents like scanned invoices, receipts, or photos.

path.description: File path (absolute). The workspace is at /Users/dev/projects/my-app

function.name: write_file
function.description: Request to write content to a file. This tool is primarily used for **creating new files** or for scenarios where a **complete rewrite of an existing file is intentionally required**. If the file exists, it will be overwritten. If it doesn't exist, it will be created. This tool will automatically create any directories needed to write the file.

path.description: The path of the file to write to (absolute). The workspace is at /Users/dev/projects/my-app

content.description: The content to write to the file. When performing a full rewrite of an existing file or creating a new one, ALWAYS provide the COMPLETE intended content of the file, without any truncation or omissions. You MUST include ALL parts of the file, even if they haven't been modified. Do NOT include the line numbers in the content though, just the actual content of the file.

line_count.description: The number of lines you intend to write. Compute this as a prediction of your full intended output before generating the content parameter. Used to detect truncation on large files (100+ lines).

function.name: apply_diff
function.description:
Request to apply PRECISE, TARGETED modifications to an existing file by searching for specific sections of content and replacing them. This streaming tool is for SURGICAL EDITS ONLY - specific changes to existing code.
You can perform multiple distinct search and replace operations within a single undefined call by providing multiple SEARCH/REPLACE blocks in the diff parameter. This is the preferred way to make several targeted changes efficiently.
The SEARCH section must exactly match existing content including whitespace and indentation.
If you're not confident in the exact content to search for, use the read_file tool first to get the exact content.
When applying the diffs, be extra careful to remember to change any closing brackets or other syntax that may be affected by the diff farther down in the file.
ALWAYS make as many changes in a single undefined call as possible using multiple SEARCH/REPLACE blocks

Diff format:
```
<<<<<<< SEARCH
:start_line: (required) The line number of original content where the search block starts.
-------
[exact content to find including whitespace]
=======
[new content to replace with]
>>>>>>> REPLACE
```


Diff examples:

Original file:
```
1 | def calculate_total(items):
2 |     total = 0
3 |     for item in items:
4 |         total += item
5 |     return total
```

Search/Replace content:
```
<<<<<<< SEARCH
:start_line:1
-------
def calculate_total(items):
    total = 0
    for item in items:
        total += item
    return total
=======
def calculate_total(items):
    """Calculate total with 10% markup"""
    return sum(item * 1.1 for item in items)
>>>>>>> REPLACE
```

Search/Replace content with multiple edits:
```
<<<<<<< SEARCH
:start_line:1
-------
def calculate_total(items):
    sum = 0
=======
def calculate_sum(items):
    sum = 0
>>>>>>> REPLACE

<<<<<<< SEARCH
:start_line:4
-------
        total += item
    return total
=======
        sum += item
    return sum
>>>>>>> REPLACE
```

path.description: The path of the file to modify (absolute). The workspace is at /Users/dev/projects/my-app

diff.description: The search/replace block defining the changes.

function.name: search_and_replace
function.description:
Use this tool to find and replace specific text strings or patterns (using regex) within a file. It's suitable for targeted replacements across multiple locations within the file. Supports literal text and regex patterns, case sensitivity options, and optional line ranges.

Notes:
- When use_regex is true, the search parameter is treated as a regular expression pattern
- When ignore_case is true, the search is case-insensitive regardless of regex mode

path.description: The path of the file to modify (absolute). The workspace is at /Users/dev/projects/my-app

search.description: The text or pattern to search for

replace.description: The text to replace matches with

start_line.description: Starting line number for restricted replacement (1-based)

end_line.description: Ending line number for restricted replacement (1-based)

use_regex.description: Set to "true" to treat search as a regex pattern (default: false)

ignore_case.description: Set to "true" to ignore case when matching (default: false)

function.name: insert_content
function.description: Use this tool specifically for adding new lines of content into a file without modifying existing content. Specify the line number to insert before, or use line 0 to append to the end. Ideal for adding imports, functions, configuration blocks, log entries, or any multi-line text block.

path.description: File path (absolute). The workspace is at /Users/dev/projects/my-app

line.description: Line number where content will be inserted (1-based). Use 0 to append at end of file. Use any positive number to insert before that line

content.description: The content to insert at the specified line

function.name: execute_command
function.description:
Request to execute a CLI command on the system. Use this when you need to perform system operations or run specific commands to accomplish any step in the user's task. You must tailor your command to the user's system and provide a clear explanation of what the command does. Prefer to execute complex CLI commands over creating executable scripts, as they are more flexible and easier to run.

If directed by the user, you may open a terminal in a different directory by using the `cwd` parameter. For long-running processes such as servers (`npm run dev`), watchers (`tsc --watch`), or daemons, set `background: true`: the process is started, its stdout and stderr are redirected to a log file, and the tool returns immediately with the process pid and the log file path (read it later with read_file). For commands known to take longer than the default timeout (e.g. large installs or builds), use the `timeout_seconds` parameter — set it to the minimum time reasonably needed, not an arbitrarily large value.

command.description: The CLI command to execute. This should be valid for the current operating system. Ensure the command is properly formatted and does not contain any harmful instructions.

cwd.description: The working directory to execute the command in (absolute). Omit to use the workspace root (/Users/dev/projects/my-app).

timeout_seconds.description: Override the default undefineds timeout for known slow commands (e.g. large installs, builds, test suites). Must be set to the minimum time reasonably needed — do not set arbitrarily large values. Maximum allowed: undefineds. Invalid or missing values default to undefineds.

function.name: grep
function.description: Fast content search using regex patterns. Returns file paths with line numbers and matching lines, sorted by modification time. Use for quickly finding which files contain a pattern. Caps at undefined matches. Results are grouped by file with line numbers.

pattern.description: Regex pattern to search for in file contents (uses Rust regex syntax).

path.description: File or directory path to search in (absolute). The workspace is at /Users/dev/projects/my-app. Accepts single path only. Defaults to workspace root.

invert_match.description: Return lines that do NOT match the pattern (-v).

word_regexp.description: Only match whole words — pattern must be surrounded by word boundaries (-w).

files_with_matches.description: Return only file paths instead of individual matching lines (-l). Useful for checking which files contain a pattern.

function.name: glob
function.description: Fast file pattern matching. Returns file paths matching a glob pattern, sorted by modification time. Use for finding files by name pattern (e.g. "**/*.ts", "src/**/*.test.ts"). Caps at undefined results.

path.description: Directory to search in (absolute). The workspace is at /Users/dev/projects/my-app. Defaults to workspace root.

function.name: list_files
function.description: Request to list files and directories within the specified directory. If recursive is true, it will list all files and directories recursively. If recursive is false or not provided, it will only list the top-level contents. Do not use this tool to confirm the existence of files you may have created, as the user will let you know if the files were created successfully or not.

path.description: The path of the directory to list contents for (absolute). The workspace is at /Users/dev/projects/my-app. Use "." to list the workspace root.

recursive.description: Whether to list files recursively. Use true for recursive listing, false or omit for top-level only.

function.name: ask_followup_question
function.description: Ask the user a question to gather additional information needed to complete the task. Use when you need clarification or more details to proceed effectively. Follow-up questions run one at a time: call this tool at most once per assistant turn and wait for the user's response before asking another question. Supports single or multiple selection mode.

question.description: A clear, specific question addressing the information needed

suggestion_a.description: Suggestion must be complete, actionable answers without placeholders.

suggestion_b.description: Suggestion must be complete, actionable answers without placeholders.

suggestion_c.description: Suggestion must be complete, actionable answers without placeholders.

suggestion_d.description: Suggestion must be complete, actionable answers without placeholders.

allow_multiple.description: Allow the user to select multiple options. Defaults to false for single selection.

function.name: use_skill
function.description: Activate a skill by name to load its full instructions into context. Only call this once per skill per current context window. If context was compacted and you need the instructions again, you may re-activate the skill.

skill_name.description: The name of the skill to activate

function.name: switch_mode
function.description: Switch to a different mode to access different capabilities and tools. Each mode is optimized for specific types of tasks.

mode_id.description: The ID of the mode to switch to

function.name: update_todo_list
function.description: Replace the entire TODO list with an updated checklist reflecting the current state. Always provide the full list; the system will overwrite the previous one. This tool is designed for step-by-step task tracking, allowing you to confirm completion of each step before updating, update multiple task statuses at once (e.g., mark one as completed and start the next), and dynamically add new todos discovered during long or complex tasks.

todos.description:
A list of tasks. Use a single-level markdown checklist (no nesting or subtasks). List todos in the intended execution order.

** Status options **
[ ] Task description (pending)
[x] Task description (completed)
[-] Task description (in progress)

**Core Principles:**
- Before updating, always confirm which todos have been completed since the last update.
- You may update multiple statuses in a single update (e.g., mark the previous as completed and the next as in progress).
- When a new actionable item is discovered during a long or complex task, add it to the todo list immediately.
- Do not remove any unfinished todos unless explicitly instructed.
- Always retain all unfinished tasks, updating their status as needed.
- Only mark a task as completed when it is fully accomplished (no partials, no unresolved dependencies).
- Only mark a task as [-] in-progress at the exact moment you begin working on it — never ahead of time to signal intent.
- When inserting a newly discovered task, only insert it — never change the status of any other existing task in that same call unless you actually did that work.
- Never remove or reword a previously [x] completed item.
- If a task is blocked, keep it as in_progress and add a new todo describing what needs to be resolved.
- Remove tasks only if they are no longer relevant or if the user requests deletion.

**Usage Example:**
<undefined>
<todos>
[x] Analyze requirements
[x] Design architecture
[-] Implement core logic
[ ] Write tests
[ ] Update documentation
</todos>
</undefined>

*After completing "Implement core logic" and starting "Write tests":
<undefined>
<todos>
[x] Analyze requirements
[x] Design architecture
[x] Implement core logic
[-] Write tests
[ ] Update documentation
[ ] Add performance benchmarks
</todos>
</undefined>

**When to Use:**
- When a todo item is completed.
- The task is complicated or involves multiple steps or requires ongoing tracking.
- You need to update the status of several todos at once.
- New actionable items are discovered during task execution.
- The user requests a todo list or provides multiple tasks.
- The task is complex and benefits from clear, stepwise progress tracking.

**When NOT to Use:**
- There is only a single, trivial task.
- The task can be completed in one or two simple steps.
- The request is purely conversational or informational.
- Do not call this tool just to mark a task [-] in-progress before starting work — only set [-] in the same update that marks the previous task [x] done. Exception: the very first task may be marked [-] in a standalone call before any task has been completed.

**Task Management Guidelines:**
- Mark task as completed immediately after all work of the current task is done.
- Mark the next task as in_progress in the same update — not in a separate call beforehand.
- Add new todos as soon as they are identified.
- Use clear, descriptive task names.

function.name: spawn_subagent
function.description: Spawn an independent subagent to handle a focused task. The subagent runs in its own isolated context and returns a summary when done. Set fork_context=true to pass the parent conversation history into the subagent when it needs prior context. Use only for clearly self-contained side work whose result can be summarized back. Do not use for simple searches, file reads, quick lookups, or work the parent agent must directly integrate. Multiple spawn_subagent calls in one turn run in parallel. Subagents cannot spawn other subagents.

description.description: What the subagent should accomplish. Be specific about what the subagent should do.

name.description: Subagent name: "general". Default: "general" or just omit the parameter for the default.

fork_context.description: When true, the parent conversation history is passed into the subagent's initial context. Use when the subagent needs to understand prior discussion, decisions, or discovered information. Default: false

function.name: start_subtask
function.description: This will let you create a new task instance using your provided title, message, and initial todo list. The title is used for display in the UI (task breadcrumbs), while the message contains the detailed instructions. Subtasks run one at a time: call this tool at most once per assistant turn.

title.description: A short title for this subtask (used for display in the UI).

message.description: The initial user message or instructions for this new task.

todos.description:
The initial todo list in markdown checklist format for the new task.
[ ] Task description (pending)
[x] Task description (completed)
[-] Task description (in progress)

mode.description: The mode ID to use for this subtask (e.g., "agent", "plan"). If not provided, defaults to "agent".

function.name: office_edit
function.description: Edit a .docx, .xlsx, or .pptx file using OfficeCLI. Supports set (update element properties), add (insert elements), remove (delete elements), move (reorder/reparent elements), find_replace (whole-document text substitution), and batch (multiple operations in one round-trip). Edits apply directly to the file; the first edit of an existing file backs it up automatically. Backup operations: restore (copy the backup back over the file), save_backup (replace the backup with the current file), delete_backup (remove the backup). Issue one call at a time — parallel calls crash the resident.

path.description: File path (absolute). The workspace is at /Users/dev/projects/my-app. Supported formats: .docx, .xlsx, .pptx

operation.description: Edit operation: "set" · "add" · "remove" · "move" · "find_replace" · "batch" (multiple operations in one round-trip — preferred when building slides or filling table rows) · "restore" · "save_backup" · "delete_backup" (manage the automatic backup; no other parameters needed).

query.description: OfficeCLI path to the target element (e.g. "/Sheet1/A1", "/body/p[1]", "/slide[1]/shape[1]"). For "add" use the parent path (e.g. "/body", "/"). For "find_replace" use "/". Not used for "batch".

props.description: JSON string of properties to apply for "set" or "add" (e.g. {"value":"Hello","bold":true} or {"type":"paragraph","text":"New line"}). Not used for "remove" or "move".

before.description: For "add"/"move": insert/place the element before this sibling DOM path (e.g. "/body/p[5]"). Mutually exclusive with "after" and "index".

after.description: For "add"/"move": insert/place the element after this sibling DOM path (e.g. "/body/p[4]"). Mutually exclusive with "before" and "index".

index.description: For "add"/"move": 0-based position within the parent (e.g. "0" = first). Mutually exclusive with "before" and "after".

to.description: For "move" only: target parent path to move the element into (e.g. "/body"). If omitted, reorders within the current parent. Inferred automatically when "before"/"after" is specified.

from.description: For "add" only: path of an existing element to clone instead of creating a new one (e.g. "/slide[1]"). Cannot be combined with "props".

ops.description: For "batch" only: JSON array of operation objects. Each object uses the same fields as a single office_edit call — "command" (set/add/remove/move), "path" or "parent", "type", "props", "before", "after", "index", "to", "from". Example: [{"command":"add","parent":"/","type":"slide"},{"command":"add","parent":"/slide[last()]","type":"shape","props":{"text":"Title","x":"2cm","y":"2cm","width":"20cm","height":"3cm"}}]

find.description: Text to search for. Required when operation is "find_replace".

replace.description: Replacement text. Required when operation is "find_replace".

function.name: FindSymbol
function.description:
Retrieves information on all symbols/code entities (classes, methods, etc.) based on the given name path pattern.
The returned symbol information can be used for edits or further queries.
Specify `depth > 0` to also retrieve children/descendants (e.g., methods of a class).

To search for a symbol in name_path_pattern, you provide a name path pattern that is used to match against name paths.
It can be
 * a simple name (e.g. "method"), which will match any symbol with that name
 * a relative path like "class/method", which will match any symbol with that name path suffix

name_path_pattern.description: The name path pattern to search for. To search for a symbol, you provide a name path pattern that is used to match against name paths.

depth.description: depth up to which descendants shall be retrieved (e.g. use 1 to also retrieve immediate children; for the case where the symbol is a class, this will return its methods). Default 0.

filter_path.description: Directory or path (relative to workspace directory /Users/dev/projects/my-app). Restrict search to this file or directory. If None, searches entire codebase. If a directory is passed, the search will be restricted to the files in that directory. If a file is passed, the search will be restricted to that file. If you have some knowledge about the codebase, you should use this parameter, as it will significantly speed up the search as well as reduce the number of results.

include_body.description: If true, include the symbol's source code. Use judiciously.

substring_matching.description: If true, use substring matching for the last element of the pattern, such that "get" would match "getValue" and "getData

function.name: create_html_artifact
function.description: Purpose: archives a static overview/summary of a larger, completed body of work as a shareable one-pager (tile with Open and Save buttons). Not a general formatter — never for code snippets/demos/tutorials (use a code block), never for diagrams (use mermaid), never for anything interactive (dashboards, forms, calculators — use file generation instead). Re-use the same id to publish a new version.

id.description: Stable snake_case identifier for this artifact (e.g. `security_findings`). Re-use the same id to publish a new version of an existing artifact.

title.description: Short human-readable title shown on the chat tile (e.g. "Security Findings").

description.description: Single-line summary shown on the chat tile under the title. Keep under 140 characters.

html.description: Full self-contained HTML document. Inline all CSS; do not reference external assets. Must start with `<` (e.g. `<!DOCTYPE html>` or `<html>`).

function.name: office_read
function.description: Read or validate a .docx, .xlsx, or .pptx file. Returns plain text, a JSON structural outline, the JSON of a specific element, an OpenXML schema validation result, or a full dump to disk for script-based analysis of large files. Issue one call at a time — parallel calls crash the resident.

path.description: File path (absolute). The workspace is at /Users/dev/projects/my-app. Supported formats: .docx, .xlsx, .pptx

mode.description: Read mode: "text" (default) · "outline" for JSON structural outline · "get" for a specific element at the query path · "validate" for OpenXML schema validation · "dump" to materialise the full document to .bob/tmp/office-dumps/ for script-based analysis.

query.description: OfficeCLI path to the element to retrieve (e.g. "/Sheet1/B2", "/body/p[1]", "/slide[1]/shape[1]"). Required when mode is "get". Optional subtree path for "dump" (defaults to "/" for whole document).

function.name: search_ibm_docs
function.description: Search IBM product documentation using semantic retrieval. Use for factual questions about IBM products, platforms, languages, commands, APIs, configuration, documented behavior, compatibility, or product-specific errors. For Bob / IBM Bob questions, use library_name `bob` directly. For other IBM products, first call list_ibm_doc_libraries and use an exact returned library name. Never invent library names.

library_name.description: Exact name returned by list_ibm_doc_libraries, or the library_name `bob` for Bob documentation. The `bob` alias is not returned by list_ibm_doc_libraries.

query.description: Optimized retrieval query with key technical terms, API names, commands, concepts, or error messages.

top_k.description: Number of results to return (default: 5, minimum: 1, maximum: 15).

function.name: create_chart
function.description: Renders an interactive ECharts chart (line, bar, pie, scatter, radar, or boxplot) as a tile in the chat. The chart is also stored as a versioned artifact — re-use the same id to publish a new version.

id.description: Stable snake_case identifier for this chart (e.g. `revenue_chart`). Re-use the same id to publish a new version of an existing chart.

type.description: Chart type: LineChart | BarChart | PieChart | ScatterChart | RadarChart | BoxplotChart

title.description: Short human-readable title shown on the chart tile.

props.description: JSON string of chart-specific props (xAxisData, series, data, etc.).

function.name: FindReferencingSymbols
function.description: Finds references to the symbol at the given `name_path_pattern`. The result will contain metadata about the referencing symbols as well as a short code snippet around the reference.

name_path_pattern.description: The name path pattern to search for. To search for a symbol, you provide a name path pattern that is used to match against name paths.

relative_path.description: File path (relative to workspace directory /Users/dev/projects/my-app). The relative path to the file containing the symbol for which to find references.
